raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: The TGAT (Temporal Graph Attention) paper proposes a temporal graph attention layer for inductive representation learning on temporal graphs, capturing temporal patterns and time-feature interactions in dynamic networks.
overlaps: Both address learning representations for temporal/dynamic graphs where node and topological features evolve over time
Both aim to capture temporal patterns and dependencies in graph data
Both produce time-aware graph/node representations
differences: TGAT uses self-attention mechanism with functional time encoding (Bochner's theorem) rather than a recurrent neural network
TGAT focuses on node-level embeddings as functions of time, whereas the novelty point describes a module that takes single-time-step graph representations and uses RNN to learn temporal dependencies
TGAT does not explicitly describe a time sequence learning module that feeds single-time-step graph representations into an RNN

sources.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
sources.quote: The evolving nature of temporal dynamic graphs requires handling new nodes as well as capturing temporal patterns.

sources.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
sources.quote: node and topological features can be temporal as well, whose patterns the node embeddings should also capture.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: The TGN (Temporal Graph Networks) paper presents a generic framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events, using memory modules and graph-based operators.
overlaps: Both address learning on dynamic/temporal graphs where connectivity and features evolve over time
Both aim to capture temporal dependencies in graph-structured data
Both target representation learning for graphs that change over time
differences: TGN uses memory modules and graph-based operators rather than a recurrent neural network for temporal learning
TGN operates on event-based dynamic graphs (sequences of timed events), whereas the novelty point describes a module that processes single-time-step graph representations through an RNN
TGN does not describe a time sequence learning module that feeds single-time-step graph representations into an RNN to learn temporal dependencies

sources.title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: few approaches have been proposed thus far for dealing with graphs that present some sort of dynamic nature (e.g. evolving features or connectivity over time).

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AliGraph is a comprehensive distributed graph neural network platform with distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to support GNN training on large-scale graph data (billions of edges).
overlaps: Distributed GNN training on large-scale graph data
Optimized sampling operators for GNN training efficiency
differences: AliGraph uses distributed graph storage rather than a leader-worker mode with edge-based graph stream partitioning
AliGraph does not employ graph summarization for mini-batch training
AliGraph does not use an attention layer to return training results to a leader node
AliGraph does not specifically target graph streaming data

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: we present a comprehensive graph neural network system, namely AliGraph, which consists of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support not only existing popular GNNs but also a series of in-house developed ones for different scenarios.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AGL is a scalable, fault-tolerant, integrated system for GNN training and inference on billion-scale graphs, using k-hop neighborhood generation and parameter server-based training.
overlaps: Distributed GNN training on large-scale graphs
Parameter server (master-worker-like) architecture for training
differences: AGL uses k-hop neighborhood subgraph generation rather than edge-based graph stream partitioning
AGL does not employ graph summarization for mini-batch training
AGL does not use an attention layer to return training results
AGL does not specifically target graph streaming data

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: we simply do the training on parameter servers due to data independency
